ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; no refund or account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the driver, who claims the rider no-showed, so the case enters via NS-0 (cancelled_by = driver with a rider no-show claim) and is decided by NS-1 [F4]. NS-1 requires (i) a tap of "I'm Here" or a platform arrival confirmation, (ii) GPS within the pickup radius at that moment, and (iii) more than 3 continuous minutes of waiting in the radius after that tap until cancellation.

On (i), the trace settles that the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 [F6]; this is a driver_tap arrival confirmation, not a platform auto-confirmation, and I record it as such [F6]. On (ii), at that tap the driver was 178 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius [F6], and his closest approach overall was 40 m [F1]. On (iii), he remained continuously within 200 m for 220 s (3 min 40 s) after the tap until cancelling, exceeding the 180 s default NS-1 threshold [F6]. The wait trace has no GPS hole (samples run from arrival confirmation to cancellation) [F2][F6], so the continuous wait is established on the record rather than inferred between samples.

The rider's assertion that the driver was not at the pin [F10] does not displace the system record: the GPS and timeline facts put the driver inside the arrival radius at the moment of the tap and for the whole wait, and system records override those statements [F1][F6]. The platform's own arrival record at 14:03:20 [F5] is not the arrival confirmation that NS-1 (i) keys on — the driver's tap at 14:06:15 is [F6] — and in any event the driver's stationary period of 4 min 0 s before cancelling [F3] also exceeds the 3-minute wait.

With (i)(ii)(iii) all satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and no refund is due under NS-1 [F4][F7]. The waiting/arrival conditions alone fix the outcome, so the fair-weather traffic facts and the profile records (driver 1 upheld no-show dispute, rider 0 upheld) [F14][F15][F16][F17][F18] are not needed and cannot decide the case on their own. This is a no-show dispute, not a safety one; no arrival-related abuse appears on the record, so no flag_account is raised [F6].

Safety screen: I read all three timestamped chat messages [F9][F10][F11][F12], the driver's written statement [F13] and the complaint. Chat #1 is a pickup arrangement ("at the side road"), Chat #2 says the rider cannot see the car, Chat #3 announces the cancellation after more than 3 minutes' wait; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in any of them, so safety_concern is none [F9][F10][F11][F13].

Evidence: the record settles every element NS-1 needs — the arrival tap, its distance from the pickup, the duration in radius, the absence of a trace hole, and the fee charged [F1][F2][F3][F4][F6][F7] — so evidence_status is sufficient and there is no gap to name.
